entries.title: The Projectionist
entries.summary: Every night for thirty years, Mara ran the last reel for an empty room. Tonight, someone stayed.
entries.body:
Every night for thirty years, Mara ran the last reel for an empty room.
The late show at the Orpheum had never been popular. By the time the credits rolled the ushers were gone, the popcorn machine had gone quiet, and the only sound in the building was the projector ticking behind her like a second heart.
She didn't mind. She liked the films better when no one was watching them. They seemed to relax.
* * *
The man in row F arrived halfway through. She saw him through the little square window: a dark shape against the silver light, hat still on, not moving.
When the reel ended she waited for him to leave. He didn't.
"We're closed," she said from the aisle.
"I know," he said. "I was waiting for the part they cut."
Mara looked at him for a long moment. Then she went back up the stairs, opened the cabinet she hadn't opened since 1994, and threaded the last reel by hand.

entries.title: Paris, Texas
entries.summary: A film about the distance between people, measured in miles and then in feet and then in nothing at all.
entries.body:
Wenders shoots the American Southwest like it's the surface of a planet nobody has bothered to name. Travis walks out of it at the start and spends the rest of the film trying to walk back into his own life.
The peep-show scene is the whole movie in miniature: two people who can't look at each other, talking through glass, finally saying the true thing because they can't see the other person's face.
Ry Cooder's slide guitar does half the acting. Harry Dean Stanton does the other half without seeming to try.

entries.title: Past Lives
entries.summary: Quiet, precise, and devastating in the way only restraint can be.
entries.body:
Nothing much happens and everything does. Celine Song trusts silence more than most first-time directors would dare, and it pays off in a final walk to a taxi that lasts about a minute and feels like twenty-four years.
